title: every cell of the table of the machine is a move the runtime takes
intent: The wave that closes the findings D1, D2 and D3 of the discriminator of waves 78 and 79, without renaming the claim of wave 78: the name of the wave, the id of the claim and the name of the check promised the coverage of a cell of the table, and wave 78 proved the coverage of a label.  The gap was real and it was demonstrated: the cell `(compacting error . failed)' was replaced with `(compacting interrupt . interrupted)', the machine could no longer move a run out of `compacting' into `failed' on the label `error', and the check of wave 78 stayed green.  Three things change.  (1) The check speaks about a cell and not about a label: for every cell of the table it says that the machine makes that move (`yeah-loop-tick' from the state of the cell answers with the state of the cell), that the runtime takes that label in a place of the code that lives, and that the cell is walked; for a label with one cell that follows from the taking of the label, and for a fan (`error', `interrupt') the fan covers exactly the states a run can live in, ends in one state, and the guard of the place of the tick does not allow a state the fan has no edge from.  (2) The check builds the graph of the reachability of the kernel: a root is an autoload cookie, a reference of `tests/' or `scripts/' or of a top-level form of `lib/', and the walk goes on by the calls -- into the arguments of a call too, because the body of a `let' is a call of the runtime like any other.  A label that only dead code takes is no longer a move the runtime takes.  (3) The label is read from the position of the label and from nowhere else, so a quoted symbol in another argument of the call is not a move of the machine.  The code of the kernel does not change: the table of wave 77 is honest, and this wave makes the proof of it match the promise.  The wave also repairs two stale places of the documentation that the discriminator named (D4) and one wrong number in the note of wave 78 (D5).
objection: The claim is amended and not rewritten: the id of the claim of wave 78 stands, and the text of the claim now says what the check proves.  The check is static, and it cannot say that a run takes every cell of the table: there is no run that meets a busy provider and grows long and waits for a person at the same time.  What it says is that the runtime has a live place where it takes every move of the table, that the machine makes every cell, and that the fan of a label covers exactly the states a run can live in.  The reachability of the kernel is a static argument: a definition that no root calls is called dead, and a definition that a root calls through a macro the reader cannot see is called dead as well -- the reader of Emacs sees the macro call and not the expansion, so a tick hidden behind a macro would be reported as missing.  The graph of the calls is an over-approximation in one direction and an under-approximation in the other: a definition that only the tests call is alive, because the tests run it, and a definition that only dead code calls is dead, because nothing runs it.  The destination of a cell is not proved against a second source: the unit test `tests/unit/test-yeah-loop.el' pins all thirty-one cells by hand and is the ground truth of the table, and the check of the wave says that the machine and the runtime walk exactly that table.  The wave does not close the gap of the state of a run (the state is not written into the journal, `docs/PLAN.md` 16.66) and does not make the reverse side of the table live: the check says that every state is reachable through the cells of the table, not that the runtime reaches it on every path.  The stale places that the discriminator named (D4) and the wrong number of the note of wave 78 (D5) are repaired here, because a document that names a range that moved is a defect of the same kind as the one the wave closes.
refuted_by: a cell of the table of the machine is not a move the machine makes, or a label of the table has no live place in the runtime where a run takes that move, or a fan of the table does not cover exactly the states a run can live in, or a cell of the table is never walked, or a state of the machine is not reachable from the first one through the cells of the table, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The claim of the wave is the claim of wave 78, amended and not rewritten.  Three controls were applied to copies of the tree on 2026-11-20 and every one of them ended with the code 1 and with the words of the check.  (1) The table: `(compacting       error         . failed)' becomes `(compacting       interrupt     . interrupted)' -- the machine loses the way out of `compacting' into `failed' on the label `error', and the check says that the fan `error' does not cover the states of a run: the table of the machine names 1 fan(s) the runtime does not keep.  (2) The dead code: the only call of `yeah-turn--retry' is renamed, so the definition of it is not reachable and the tick of the label `rate-blocked' sits in dead code -- the check says that the table of the machine names 1 move(s) that the runtime does not take: (rate-blocked), and that the cell `(deciding rate-blocked . blocked-on-rate)' is never walked.  (3) The position of the label: the quoted symbol `rate-blocked' moves into another argument of the call, out of the position of the label -- the check says the same as in the second control.  The control of wave 78 (the tick of `tool-end' taken away) bites the new check as well.  The measurement of the wave: the table of the machine has thirty-one cells, seventeen labels and eleven states; the runtime has twenty-three places where it takes a move, and all twenty-three are live; the kernel has nine hundred and eleven definitions, seventy-seven roots of reachability and seven hundred and seventy-six live definitions; the check of the wave runs in 4.6 seconds.
